newsitem.title: UK: Private healthcare to grow after election - survey.
newsitem.headline: Private healthcare to grow after election - survey.

text.p: Doctors think the demand for private healthcare in Britain will grow after Thursday's national election, a survey released on Tuesday found.
The survey of more than 2,000 surgeons at the end of last year showed 42 percent expected an increase in private patients by the end of this year, with only 17 percent expecting a drop.
The survey, carried out by healthcare consultants Griffiths Bradwell Associates, also found that most doctors thought their patients benefited from having access to private treatment.
Asked: "Overall, considering financial and other criteria, do you feel that your NHS (National Health Service) unit benefits from private practice?" 73 percent said yes.

"We hope that any new government accepts the hand of partnership from the private sector to work together to ensure freedom of choice and the highest quality of equitable healthcare for all, and not a new era of growing waiting lists because of outdated dogma," PPP healthcare group, the private insurer that released the survey, said in a statement.
The state of Britain's NHS, which many complain is overburdened, has been a hot issue in the election campaign.
